label: paragraph_title
text: THAT NEW PORT.

label: paragraph_title
text:
LOWER THAN WHAMPOA
FAVOURED?
RIVER HEAL SCHEME

label: text
text: “A certain gentleman who comes from Canton” is quoted by the vernacular papers of this morning, as having expounded a project by the Provincial Government to organise a big port at the mouth of the Canton River, further down than Whampoa.

label: text
text: At first, so the speaker is reported, the Kwangtung Government considered the Bak Ngo Taam (that part of the Canton Harbour by Shameen and leading to the "back reach") the widest anchorage. It was the intention to accommodate bigger ships at Whampoa but the water there has been found to be too shallow. Accordingly, a project is being mooted to develop the port of Tai Ping (at the head of the estuary and close to Bocca Tigris) and its suburb of Sha Kok (sometimes known as the Sha Kok Fort).

label: paragraph_title
text: STRIKE EXAMINATION

label: text
text: The Canton Admiralty has despatched the "Kong Hon" to patrol the Bocca Tigris Passage to examine incoming foreign vessels. It having been reported to the Strike Executive that merchandise is being shipped to Canton from Shanghai under changed labels special examination pickets have been added.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: YOUNG INHERITOR AND LOCAL ESTATE.

label: text
text: HIS RELATIVES AT LAW.

label: text
text: Allegations of forgery in connection with a document purporting to be a will were made in the course of a probate court case at the Supreme Court to its morning by Mr. H. S. Fitzroy, counsel for plaintiff.

label: text
text: The properties alleged to have been disposed of by this document were houses in Queen's Road and Wellington Street, Hongkong, bringing in a yearly rental of $1,300.

label: text
text: Letters of administration had already been granted in respect of the document purporting to be the will and this morning's application was for their revocation.

label: text
text: The plaintiff in the case was the grandmother of deceased (a youth of seventeen, who had inherited the property from his father and died of consumption). The defendant was the wife of deceased.

label: text
text: The grandmother states that during the time of his illness the deceased was in her room and as he was in a state of exhaustion and for a considerable time unable even to speak, no one was allowed to visit him without her permission. Neither his wife nor the parties who had sworn to be witnesses of the signature of the document purporting to be a will had visited the deceased, stated the condition.

label: text
text: The grandmother further deposes to having lived with the wife after the omination of the deceased and nothing was said for three years of there ever being a will in existence. There was difference of opinion eventually between her and the wife and the wife left. It was after this that the document was produced. An interview with another re

label: text
text: An interview with another relative which the wife is deposed

label: text
text: He will be referred to in court this morning. Mr. Fitzroy stating that the wife produced a document purporting to be the will and signed by her deceased husband. She told the relative that there had been trouble with the grandmother and wanted him to sign the document in order that they might get the property. This he declined to do and Mr. Fitzroy states that this relative recognises the document as that on which was based the grant of letters of administration.

label: text
text: The abode of the deceased at the crucial dates was Sheklung, Kwangtung province.

label: text
text: The name of the plaintiff is Li U. Shi and of the defendant, Li Soo She.

label: text
text: As the facts as outlined by Mr. Fitzroy were not contested by the defendants, the case being an ex parte one, His Lordship, Sir Henry Cowper's Gollan before whom the case was tried, found for the plaintiffs and the grant of letters of administration to the widow was revoked.

label: paragraph_title
text: BACK IN COLONY.

label: text
text: A RETURNED BANISHEE'S DOINGS.

label: text
text: SENTENCES TO FIT THE CRIME.

label: text
text: Attempting to extort money by posing as a police constable and returning from banishment were charges against a Chinese brought before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: The evidence was that a man was arrested on Sunday on a charge of being concerned in a Triad Society. Defendant, representing himself to be a constable, visited the man's home the following day and demanded $6 from his wife, stating that he would put in a good word with the police on behalf of her husband. Defendant was asked to call again for the money. The next day the husband was released and on hearing from his wife about the visitor's demand a trap was laid with the assistance of the police. When arrested he was recognised as a banisher.

label: text
text: Defendant was sentenced to three months hard labour for posing as a constable, and one year's hard labour for returning from banishment. In addition he was ordered to receive 15 strokes of the birch.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: RESIDENTS LOSE VALUABLES

label: text

label: text
text: Gaining entry by process of a bathroom which they returned by surmounting a balust alle, breaking the window and withdrawing the lower� bolt, righters away with some valuables belonging to residents of the Peak Hotel early this morning.

label: text
text: The robbery must have been effected some time between midnight and 6 a.m. (when the traces of their nocturnal visit were first reported by the Hotel boys).

label: text
text: Three rooms were entered, from room No. 58 were taken a plantinum ring with two large diamonds and eight small ones, valued at $90, and a gold wrist-watch, valued at £12, whilst a gold filled Waltham watch, full hunter, valued at $60, was taken from another room. The first mentioned ring and watch were the property of Mr. and Mrs. Kill.

label: text
text: Report, hitherto unconfirmed mentions a robbery of a diamond pin from Mr. Butterfield's room and that of a clock, the property of Dr. H. Baream but the matter is incorrect for its transferred that the clock was only moved from the mantle.

label: text
text: The police are making enquiries. The indications are that the robbers knew their way about the hotel.
